items.title: Association between sexual orientation and depression among male patients with HIV: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Wen J, Zhou S, Li K, Tang Z, Yan Y, Zhang Z.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Depression is a prevalent comorbidity among people living with HIV (PLWH) and is associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Sexual minority men may face unique psychosocial stressors that increase vulnerability to depression. This study aimed to investigate the association between sexual orientation and depression among male patients with HIV in Suqian, China.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 163 male HIV-positive patients. Sexual orientation was self-reported as heterosexuality or homosexuality. Depression was assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), analyzed both as a continuous variable and as a categorical variable (PHQ-9 ≥ 10 indicating depression). Four multivariable regression models were constructed with progressively adjusted covariates: Model 1 (unadjusted), Model 2 (sociodemographic factors), Model 3 (lifestyle factors), and Model 4 (clinical factors).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 163 participants, 91 (55.8%) identified as heterosexual and 72 (44.2%) as homosexual. Homosexual participants were significantly older (63.85 ± 12.63 vs. 46.53 ± 10.07 years) and had higher depression prevalence (22.2% vs. 11.0%). In the fully adjusted model (Model 4), homosexuality was significantly associated with increased odds of depression (OR = 4.45, 95% CI: 1.43-15.58, p  = 0.013). The association remained consistently positive across all models, though statistical significance for the continuous PHQ-9 outcome was marginal (β = 1.84, 95% CI: -0.10 to 3.78, p  = 0.063).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Homosexual orientation is independently associated with higher depression risk among male HIV patients, highlighting the need for tailored mental health screening and interventions for sexual minority men in HIV care settings.

items.title: Serum Extracellular Vesicle Proteomics Identifies Candidate Protein Biomarkers for Major Depressive Disorder with a Diagnostic Specificity Assessment against Schizophrenia.
items.authors: Fan F, Fu Q, Du Y, Liang J, Tang Q, Cheng Y, Chen Y, Xie G.

sections.text: Diagnosis of major depressive disorder (MDD) relies on subjective criteria and lacks objective biomarkers. Serum extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry stable cargo and can cross the blood-brain barrier, making them attractive biomarker sources. We therefore profiled serum EVs from a discovery cohort of 60 participants (40 healthy controls [HCs], 20 MDD patients) by size-exclusion chromatography and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and subsequently validated candidate proteins by ELISA in an independent cohort of 60 participants (20 HCs, 20 MDD, 20 patients with schizophrenia [SCZ]). Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were defined by |log2 fold change| > 1 and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted q < 0.05. Using these criteria, we identified 358 DEPs (235 upregulated, 123 downregulated), which were enriched in complement activation, coagulation, and immune-inflammatory pathways. However, several of the most significant DEPs are abundant circulating plasma proteins that are common co-isolates of serum EVs, so part of this signal may reflect residual soluble serum protein, and-given that EVs were isolated from serum rather than platelet-poor plasma-the pathway enrichment should be interpreted with caution. In the validation cohort, EV-associated TNC and APLP1 were elevated and EV-associated TF was reduced in MDD relative to HCs (P < 0.05), whereas only serum APLP1 was elevated. Notably, EV-associated TNC was also elevated in SCZ, while APLP1 and TF were unchanged; moreover, direct MDD-versus-SCZ comparisons were not significant, indicating that the data do not support MDD-specific alterations. In addition, a logistic-regression model combining EV-associated APLP1, TF and TNC distinguished MDD from HCs with an area under the curve of 0.905 (95% CI 0.812-0.998; 0.830 by leave-one-out cross-validation), outperforming individual proteins (TF 0.725; TNC 0.758; APLP1 0.725). Collectively, these findings define a serum EV-associated proteomic signature in MDD and preliminarily validate TF, TNC and APLP1 as candidate diagnostic biomarkers, implicating immune-inflammatory and complement-related pathways. Nevertheless, the panel remains exploratory and requires validation in larger, multi-center cohorts with diverse psychiatric controls.

items.title: The emotional and psychological impact of pregnancy loss before 24 weeks gestation across elapsed time and income settings: an umbrella review.
items.authors: Sekar S, Pandey A, Jijo J, Odendaal J, Quenby S, Tempest N.

sections.text: Pregnancy loss before 24 weeks gestation is common, encompassing miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy, and molar pregnancy. Research consistently demonstrates increased risks of anxiety and depression following loss. These may persist long after physical recovery, shaping future reproductive decisions. We aimed to identify, appraise, and synthesise findings on the emotional and psychological impact of pregnancy loss before 24 weeks. In this umbrella review, we searched MEDLINE (via PubMed), EMBASE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and Scopus databases from database inception to April 30, 2026 for relevant works published in English. The population of interest comprised individuals who experienced pregnancy loss before 24 weeks' gestation, including miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy, and molar pregnancy, with exposure defined as pregnancy loss itself. The primary outcomes were emotional and psychological impact following pregnancy loss before 24 weeks, including, but not limited to, depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), grief, psychological well-being, coping processes, and decisions regarding future parenting. We included systematic reviews, with or without meta-analysis, meta-synthesis, or meta-aggregation and narrative systematic reviews that examined the emotional and psychological impact of pregnancy loss before 24 weeks' gestation. Sex and gender were extracted as reported in the included systematic reviews. Methodological quality was assessed using the AMSTAR-2 tool, qualitative evidence was synthesised using the Thomas & Harden (2008) approach, evidence credibility was graded using the Fusar-Poli and Radua methodology and overlap was assessed using the corrected covered area approach. The protocol for this review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO, CRD420251142534. The literature search identified 474 records. After removal of duplicates and relevance screening, 32 full texts were screened, of which 12 were excluded. Of the 20 included reviews, eight were rated as high quality, nine as low quality, and three as critically low quality according to AMSTAR 2. Five reviews focused on qualitative synthesis, 12 on quantitative synthesis, and three adopted mixed-methods approaches. Quantitative evidence was available for depression, anxiety, stress, grief, and PTSD, while qualitative evidence explored experiences following pregnancy loss. The findings from these 20 systematic reviews, incorporating 260 unique primary studies, demonstrated that pregnancy loss before 24 weeks is associated with substantial emotional and psychological morbidity, particularly pronounced burdens were observed in low-income and middle-income settings, in the acute phase (<3 months) following loss, although elevated risks frequently persist beyond 12 months. Further research is needed to determine how these emotional and psychological needs can be identified and addressed effectively. However, conclusions are limited by substantial heterogeneity and study overlap, and evidence for ectopic and molar pregnancy remained limited in both quantitative and qualitative syntheses. None.

items.title: Neuropsychiatric outcomes after decompressive craniectomy and cranioplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Bari SSM, Behnam P, Saghebdoust S, Simon N, Uff C, Jamjoom AAB.

sections.text: Neuropsychiatric morbidity after decompressive craniectomy (DC) is increasingly recognised, but prevalence and trajectories remain unclear. We aimed to examine psychiatric and cognitive outcomes post-DC. The systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO-CRD 420251106085) followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Medline, Embase, PsycINFO, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases were searched through October 2025. Eligible studies included validated psychometric and cognitive tools to assess psychiatric and cognitive outcomes post-DC. The Random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate the pooled prevalence. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², and meta-regression explored sources of variability. Longitudinal outcomes after cranioplasty were analysed separately. Twenty-four studies were included in the qualitative analysis (N = 877), and 12 were included in the meta-analysis (N = 305). The pooled prevalence of depression was 47% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 40-54%, I²=20.2% [95% CI: 0-58.9%]), and anxiety, from four studies, was 46% (95% CI: 38-54%, I²=0% [95% CI: 0-84.7%]). Limited longitudinal data available from two studies showed a reduction in anxiety and depression after cranioplasty, with large effect sizes at 12 months (anxiety: p < 0.001, g = 5.36; depression: p < 0.001, g = 5.04). However, the effect sizes may have been inflated due to small cohorts included in these studies. Among the six studies reporting severity, the rates of moderate depression ranged from 8.3​​% to 45.5%, and severe depression from 9.1% to 36.4% across assessment tools. Most of the included studies showed improved cognitive outcome post-cranioplasty, however quantitative analysis was not possible due to varied study design. A considerable proportion of post-DC patients experience depression and anxiety. Selective screening can improve early detection and resource allocation. Future studies should focus on developing targeted patient pathways.

items.title: Prevalence of Depression, Anxiety, Stress and Insomnia Among Healthcare Workers in Saudi Arabia During COVID-19: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Review and Random-Effects Meta-Analysis.
items.authors: Mathkor DM, Irshad M, Shaikh MF, Haque S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The outbreak of SARS-CoV-2 placed healthcare workers (HCWs) under substantial psychological burden. Despite many Saudi studies, no pooled national estimate of mental health problems among HCWs during COVID-19 has been reported.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to synthesize existing evidence using PRISMA guidelines to estimate the pooled prevalence of mental health problems among HCWs in Saudi Arabia during COVID-19.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Systematic searches on selected online web-databases identified eligible cross-sectional studies of HCWs in Saudi Arabia (data collected between 1 March 2020 to 30 March 2021) reporting prevalence of depression, anxiety, stress, psychological distress, or insomnia using validated tools with established cut-off scores. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated pooled prevalence, while study quality and heterogeneity were examined using the JBI checklist/itemized risk-of-bias and I^2 statistic.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Thirty-six studies involving 20,787 HCWs met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of depression (n = 10,452) was 50.2% (95% CI: 38.5 - 61.8; I^2 = 98.4), anxiety (n = 12,692) was 58.1% (95% CI: 50.4 - 65.3; I^2 = 98.0%), stress (n = 5,181) was 63.9% (95% CI: 39.8 - 82.6; I^2 = 98.4%), psychological distress (n = 6,647) was 57.0% (95% CI: 34.3 - 77.1; I^2 = 99.3%), and insomnia (n = 3,108) was 57.3% (95% CI: 34.1 - 77.7; I^2 = 99.0). The pooled prevalence of moderate-to-severe depression was 24.0% (95% CI: 16.0 - 35.0; I^2 = 98.6%), anxiety 35.8% (95% CI: 28.1 - 44.2, I^2 = 98.7%), stress 48.6% (95% CI: 24.2 - 73.7; I^2 = 98.9%), psychological distress 27.3% (95% CI: 13.6 - 47.3; I^2 = 98.8%) and insomnia 13.4% (95% CI: 7.9 - 21.7, I^2 = 80.2) among HCWs.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Most of HCWs experienced mental health problems during COVID-19, with stress being the most prevalent condition, highlighting the need for preventive and supportive mental health strategies during public health emergencies.

items.title: Body and Movement Based Interventions in Psychotic Disorders: A Scoping Review of Treatments and Outcomes
ACT now: a mixed-methods evaluation of a nurse-led tobacco treatment program in a safety-net hospital.
items.authors: Ngo TP, Skinner SN, Benowitz N, Martin M, Vijayaraghavan M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Tobacco use remains prevalent among patients hospitalized in safety-net settings, where co-occurring psychosocial and structural needs complicate treatment and contribute to persistent health disparities. However, little is known about how nurse-led tobacco treatment programs within addiction consult services are implemented, prioritized, and sustained. This study estimated tobacco use prevalence and correlates and examined multilevel factors influencing the implementation and sustainability of a novel licensed vocational nurse-led inpatient tobacco treatment model designed for resource-constrained safety-net settings.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We used a convergent mixed-methods design, guided by PRISM and RE-AIM frameworks, integrating retrospective electronic health record data with qualitative interviews in an urban safety-net hospital. Quantitative analyses included adults with index hospitalizations ≥ 24 h between August 1, 2019, and December 31, 2023 (n = 38,068). We obtained qualitative data using semi-structured interviews with hospitalized patients receiving Addiction Care Team services (n = 20) and clinical staff and leadership (n = 10) and analyzed them thematically. We integrated quantitative and qualitative data to confirm and expand on findings.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Current tobacco use was identified in 7,950 individuals (20.9%) and declined from 25.0% in 2019 to 18.3% in 2023. Tobacco use was associated with non-tobacco substance use disorder (aOR = 3.26, 95% CI = 3.06-3.48), discharge from psychiatric versus obstetric/gynecologic services (aOR = 2.94, 95% CI = 2.47-3.49), homelessness (aOR = 1.56, 95% CI = 1.45-1.67), and self-directed discharge (aOR = 1.37, 95% CI = 1.22-1.54). Qualitative findings explained these patterns, highlighting how competing priorities, workflow constraints, and structural barriers shape tobacco treatment delivery. items.title: Health outcomes in cancer survivors living alone vs. living with family: a multinational survey study.
items.authors: Sim AH, Lee J, Kim S, Shin DW, Cho J, Kang D.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: With an increasing number of individuals living alone, it is important to understand its impact on health outcomes in cancer survivors. However, previous studies have not sufficiently considered variations in age, sex, and survival period, even though these are important effect modifiers. This study aims to determine whether cancer survivors living alone have worse general and mental health outcomes compared to those living with family.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A multinational cross-sectional study used data from the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) and Korean NHANES (KNHANES) from 2007 to 2021, including 6,400 cancer survivors (1,198 living alone and 5,202 living with family). The primary outcomes were general health status and mental health (limitations on daily activities due to emotional problems and suicidal ideation).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Cancer survivors living alone had higher odds for poor/fair general health than survivors living with family (aOR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.14-1.56). Regarding health behaviors, those living alone were slightly more likely to be current smokers and to have comorbidities. Furthermore, those living alone had significantly higher odds of limitations on daily activities due to emotional problems (aOR, 3.99; 95% CI, 1.49-10.68) and suicidal ideation (aOR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.03-2.05) than those living with family. The association was strongest in those younger than 40 years (P for interaction = 0.01) and in survivors diagnosed within 1 year (P for interaction < 0.01).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Cancer survivors living alone experience significantly worse general and mental health outcomes, particularly younger survivors and those in the early post-diagnosis period, suggesting the need for further longitudinal research to clarify the underlying mechanisms.

items.title: Understanding stakeholder views on dialectical behavior therapy for post-traumatic stress disorder: a qualitative analysis of clinician and patient experiences.
items.authors: Nadeau L, Larrivée É, Paré AS, Therriault C, Taillefer A, Charest F, Hudon A, Bérubé FA, Cailhol L.
items.journal: Borderline personality disorder and emotion dysregulation

sections.text: Individuals with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) and Complex Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (C-PTSD) often face significant challenges in treatment due to the severity and complexity of their symptoms. Dialectical Behavior Therapy for PTSD (DBT-PTSD) is a phase-based, multicomponent psychotherapy developed to address the needs of this population. sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This qualitative study explored the perspectives of six patients and five clinicians involved in DBT-PTSD at a university-affiliated mental health institute. Data were collected through individual interviews and focus groups at multiple time points and were analyzed inductively using Reflexive Thematic Analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Five themes were generated, including trauma-focused exposure as a main mechanism of change, the role of the therapeutic alliance in supporting engagement and treatment outcomes, the demanding nature of trauma-focused exposure, the tension between fidelity and flexibility within the protocol, and the influence of individual resources on patients' experiences with at-home assignments.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This is the first study to qualitatively examine DBT-PTSD, providing insights into its perceived relevance, challenges, and potential impact. These findings may contribute to clinical training, guide adaptations of the protocol, and contribute to refining trauma interventions for individuals with BPD and C-PTSD.

items.title: First-Episode Psychosis in a Patient With Flaccid Paraplegia Following Childhood Poliomyelitis.
items.authors: Coelho JT, Ramos AL, Felgueiras J, Timóteo S, Salgado H.

sections.text: First-episode psychosis in patients with pre-existing neurological disability presents important diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when the relationship between the two conditions is uncertain. This case report describes a 49-year-old man with flaccid paraplegia following childhood poliomyelitis who was involuntarily admitted for a first documented acute psychotic episode. His presentation included behavioural disorganisation, self-neglect, aggression, disorganised speech, and persecutory delusions. Initial laboratory investigations, including a complete blood count, inflammatory markers, electrolytes, glucose, and renal and hepatic function tests, were unremarkable. Urine toxicology screening was negative for the substances tested, while cranial computed tomography and neuropsychological assessment did not reveal acute structural abnormalities or major cognitive impairment that could explain the psychotic symptoms. However, more extensive neurological investigations were not performed. Clinical improvement was achieved with oral aripiprazole followed by long-acting injectable aripiprazole, alongside coordinated psychiatric and social support. This case highlights the importance of avoiding unsupported causal assumptions between remote neurological disease and new-onset psychosis, while recognising the diagnostic limitations of the available investigations. It also illustrates how chronic physical disability and psychosocial vulnerability can complicate psychiatric management, making multidisciplinary care essential for treatment continuity and functional stability.

items.title: A national environmental scan of postvention services in Veterans Affairs healthcare systems.
items.authors: Sears MS, Higgins EL, Harvey ME, Lalka A, Matarazzo BB.

sections.text: Suicide loss impacts up to six million Americans annually and is associated with increased suicidal ideation and mental health conditions among survivors. Postvention is an innovative public health intervention for suicide prevention that provides organized support services to loss survivors. U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) healthcare facilities have developed local postvention services that may serve as blueprints for healthcare settings at large. The structure, breadth, and types of services provided at these facilities, however, have never been assessed or described. This environmental scan surveyed all 140 VA healthcare facilities nationwide to describe existing postvention services. Facilities were classified post-hoc as high-service (providing support across broader circumstances and to a wider range of survivors), and limited-service. Barriers and facilitators to implementation and structural components were examined as predictors of service category. Most facilities (88%) reported having postvention response processes in place. Support for both loved ones and VA employees was available at over 90% of facilities following suicide deaths; just over half offered support to impacted veterans. Eighty-three percent of facilities reported the ability to provide postvention following veteran suicides, 53% following employee suicides, and 59% in the rare event that a suicide occurs on a VA campus. A total of 26% of facilities met the criteria for a high-service facility. Facilities with written standard operating procedures (SOPs), leadership support, and staff interest in postvention were more likely to be high-service facilities; those that perceived low suicide rates in their region to be a barrier to postvention implementation tended to offer fewer postvention services. A multivariable model found that facilities with written SOPs still had greater odds of being high-service facilities after controlling for leadership buy-in and staff interest, whereas the latter two variables were not independently associated with high-service status. VA postvention programs varied considerably in structure and scope, though proactive advance planning and outreach to both loved ones and staff were common features. Future implementation efforts could include assisting facilities with documenting their postvention preparation plans in written SOPs, broadening interdisciplinary engagement in providing postvention services, and engaging leadership support.

items.title: Adolescent depression in Chinese schools and families: a case study of 20 adolescents.
items.authors: Wang X, Suttawet C.

sections.text: This study examines adolescent depression within Chinese families and educational environments through an action research approach, engaging researchers and practitioners in continuous cycles of observation, intervention, and reflection. Within this iterative process, direct counselling sessions and family therapy were deployed as active intervention mechanisms alongside the qualitative analysis of 20 depressed individuals aged 13 to 22. The findings indicate that adolescent depression emerges from a complex interplay of academic pressures and socio-environmental stressors. Family dysfunction-particularly parental separation and emotionally volatile parenting-frequently serves as a primary root cause, compounded by severe academic competition and peer rejection. Notably, female and middle school participants exhibited heightened vulnerability, with nearly half of the cohort utilizing non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) to cope with emotional distress. To bridge existing care gaps, the study proposes a collaborative, ecosystemic intervention model integrating families, schools, medical systems, and peer networks. Furthermore, policymakers are encouraged to establish national mental health registries, mandate standardized school-based screenings, and provide targeted subsidies to support long-term adolescent recovery and resilience.

items.title: Latent profile analysis of sleep quality and associated factors in Chinese adolescents with major depressive disorder.
items.authors: Hu Y, Shen Y, Zeng C, Qiu J, Wu Q, Li Y, Liu D.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Sleep disturbances are pervasive among adolescent patients with major depressive disorder (MDD), yet the heterogeneity of sleep phenotypes within this population remains underexplored. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of sleep quality in Chinese adolescent patients with MDD and to examine their associations with sociodemographic, clinical, and psychosocial factors.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 1,467 adolescent patients with MDD were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Borderline Personality Features Scale for Children (BPFS-C), and a self-designed sociodemographic and clinical inventory. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was conducted using the seven PSQI component scores as profile indicators. Multinomial logistic regression was subsequently performed to determine factors associated with profile membership.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A five-profile solution was identified: Normal Sleep Group (13%), Mild Disturbance-Low Hypnotic Use (36%), Mild Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use (22%), Severe Disturbance-Low Hypnotic Use (16%), and Severe Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use (13%). Logistic regression revealed that the presence of non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) and exposure to negative life events significantly increased the odds of belonging to more severe sleep disturbance profiles ( OR  = 2.92-8.37 and 2.33-2.60, respectively; all p < 0.05). Notably, patients without left-behind experiences exhibited higher odds of being classified into the Severe Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use profile compared to those with such histories ( OR  = 0.46, p  < 0.001). Furthermore, profiles characterized by poorer sleep quality and profiles characterized by more frequent self-reported sleep medication use were cross-sectionally associated with greater anxiety and borderline features in this study.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Sleep quality among adolescent patients with MDD exhibits distinct typological heterogeneity, characterized primarily by severity and hypnotic use patterns. These findings provide preliminary exploratory evidence for the development of personalized, profile-informed clinical interventions for this vulnerable population.

items.title: Substance dependence: distinct transcriptomic patterns and neuroimmune system involvement in addiction pathogenesis and progression.
items.authors: Yakovchik A, Spektor E, Mamchur A, Zelenova Е, Ivanov M, Kashtanova D, Matkava L, Terekhov M, Tarasova D, Petrova V, Pavlov K, Pavlova O, Nebogina K, Vyshinsky K, Kozlov A, Shport S, Yudin V, Keskinov А, Yudin S, Skvortsova V.

sections.text: It is well-established that consistent exposure to psychoactive substances can alter gene expression within the brain's reward and motivation centers. These lasting changes in neuronal gene expression, including those driven by transcriptional mechanisms, can lead to a persistent craving for these substances, resulting in a definitive loss of behavioral control over consumption. Examining transcriptome alterations in individuals with established addiction may provide valuable insight into the mechanisms underlying addiction; however, research remains limited. Utilizing peripheral blood samples rather than solely postmortem brain tissues to evaluate gene expression changes may offer significant clinical benefits. We examined data from a cohort of patients addicted to alcohol and other psychoactive substances, including their drug use histories, psychometric status, and personality traits. We performed differential gene expression analysis to identify general and addiction-specific changes in peripheral blood transcriptomes in participants with different types of addiction. We detected patterns of expression changes in peripheral blood characteristic of addictions to psychoactive substances. Some of the changes were reflective of the overall pathological processes occurring in individuals with chronic substance use disorders. However, other changes, such as the hyperexpression of genes and dysregulation of functional pathways associated with the immune-inflammatory responses, may be indicative of the development of neuroinflammation and may illuminate its role in addiction development. Changes in specific RNA levels could explain pathological processes occurring during chronic substance use. The identified candidate molecular markers of addiction in peripheral blood could contribute to enhanced diagnostic capabilities and facilitate the development of personalized treatment strategies. However, these peripheral blood findings lack functional or causal verification, representing candidate transcriptomic associations rather than confirmed molecular markers.

items.title: Psychiatric Services Following Suicide-Related Hospital Visits: An Analysis of Electronic Health Records Among Patients With Depression.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Prompt psychiatric follow-up after suicidal events can improve outcomes, but factors associated with timely care remain uncertain.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using electronic health records, we identified adults with hospitalizations or emergency department (ED) visits for suicidal ideation, self-harm, or suicide attempt between January 2021 and June 2024 among patients with depression. We estimated the odds of completed outpatient psychiatric follow-up within 30 days, assessed the association between hospitalization length and prior health system engagement, and evaluated the odds of the first appointment being conducted via telehealth.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 5111 patients discharged to home or self-care following a suicide-related ED visit or hospitalization, 11.9% completed outpatient psychiatric follow-up within 30 days of discharge. Patients without prior-year engagement discharged after an ED visit or short stay had lower predicted probabilities of follow-up than patients with prior-year engagement or longer stays. Telehealth follow-up was more common among patients with prior engagement and less common among patients residing in low Area Deprivation Index areas.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Outpatient psychiatric follow-up completion after suicidal events was low, particularly among patients without prior health system engagement and those with shorter index admissions. Targeted follow-up interventions for these groups may improve timely psychiatric care.

sections.text: Low psychiatric follow-up appointment completion after suicide-related events underscores the need for further attention to discharge planning and coordination for patients with depression.

items.title: Study protocol: efficacy and safety of Limosilactobacillus fermentum WIS32 as an adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder-a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
items.authors: Xiang Q, Yan Z, Duan Y, Li M, Sheng L, Chai X, Ma Y, Cai F, Li Y, Liu Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. Although antidepressant medications are widely used as first-line treatments, a substantial proportion of patients experience insufficient therapeutic response or limited tolerability, highlighting the need for additional safe and effective adjunctive treatment strategies. In recent years, growing evidence has suggested that the microbiota-gut-brain axis may play an important modulatory role in the onset, maintenance, and treatment response of depression.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Limosilactobacillus fermentum WIS32, a human breast milk-derived probiotic strain, as an adjunctive intervention to stable antidepressant therapy in patients with MDD, and to further explore its potential effects on selected biological markers.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. A total of 86 patients with MDD diagnosed according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5), are required to complete the study. Allowing for an anticipated dropout rate, 108 participants will be recruited. All participants will continue stable antidepressant treatment and will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either Limosilactobacillus fermentum WIS32 or a matched placebo for 8 weeks. The primary outcome is the change in the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) score from baseline to week 8.

sections.heading: Trial status
sections.text: This manuscript describes protocol version 1.0, dated 8 April 2025. The trial was prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500100388) on 8 April 2025, a WHO ICTRP Primary Registry, which collects and publicly displays the WHO Trial Registration Data Set (TRDS). Participant recruitment began on 10 June 2025 and is ongoing at the time of submission. Recruitment is expected to be completed by December 2026.

items.title: Test anxiety and satisfaction with studies: the mediating role of academic engagement in university students.
items.authors: Ramos-Gonzales NE, Zuñiga-Aranda RR, Cunza-Aranzábal DF.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: This study, based on the Control-Value Theory (CVT) and enhanced by the Study Demands-Resources (SD-R) framework (an adaptation of the Job Demands-Resources model to academic contexts), analyzed the structural relationships among test anxiety, academic engagement, and satisfaction with studies among Peruvian university students. The research particularly concentrated on the role of engagement in clarifying this relationship.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: A cross-sectional associative design incorporating latent variables was utilized. The sample comprised 522 students with a mean age of 20.6 years and a standard deviation of 2.17. Standardized instruments, namely TAI-State, UWES-3S, and BSSWS, were employed. Data analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with the WLSMV estimator.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The measurement model showed satisfactory reliability (α, ω > .700) and validity. The structural model demonstrated an adequate fit: Scaled χ^2(186) = 585.919; p < .001; CFI = .973, TLI = .969; RMSEA = .064, 90% CI [.058,.070]; SRMR = .048. Results indicated that test anxiety is negatively associated with satisfaction (β = - .154, p = .001) and academic engagement (β = - .172, p < .001). Academic engagement is positively associated with satisfaction (β = .674, p < .001) and statistically accounts for 37.32% of the total association between anxiety and satisfaction. The model proved invariant across gender and university type.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Statistical analysis indicates that academic engagement significantly contributes to the relationship between achievement emotions and student satisfaction. These findings imply that university support strategies may be enhanced by integrating re-engagement methods in conjunction with anxiety reduction to promote student well-being.

items.title: Psychological adjustment under dual pressures: a bibliometric analysis of the impact of academic stress and employment anxiety on college students' mental health.
items.authors: Gong Y, Zhang X, Li D, Lau AD.

sections.text: Mental health of College students has long been a critical research topic in higher education and psychological research. Academic pressure and employment anxiety are the primary stressors that affect their psychological adaptation. To overcome the lack of objectivity and systematicity in existing literature reviews, this study takes the core databases of CNKI and Web of Science as data sources. It adopts CiteSpace, VOSviewer and other analytical tools to conduct bibliometric analysis and knowledge graph visualization. This research intends to map the evolutionary trajectory, academic collaboration landscape and intellectual structure of this research field, and further explore the value of bibliometric methods in supporting the localized revision of stress theories. The findings reveal notable disparities between domestic research trajectories and those of Chinese scholars' English-language publications. Domestic studies have formed a dual-dominant framework revolving around academy and employment, whereas international scholarship primarily focuses on general psychological mechanisms. Academic collaboration networks across the field remain loosely connected. The Cognitive Appraisal Theory of Stress serves as the mainstream theoretical foundation. Additionally, research paradigms are gradually shifting toward positive psychology, and the prominent emergence of psychological resilience provides quantitative evidence for theoretical revision. This study establishes a localized theoretical model labeled dual stress-cognitive appraisal-resilience buffering, which achieves dynamic optimization and localized adaptation of classical stress theories. From a macro bibliometric perspective, this paper remedies the shortcomings of traditional reviews, and provides scientific implications for addressing dual stress at the source and implementing targeted mental health interventions for College students.

items.title: The nonlinear relationship between symptoms of internet addiction and depressive symptoms: an empirical study among Chinese university students.
items.authors: Peng S, Sali A, Qingpo H, Zhang P.

sections.heading: Object
sections.text: To examine the nonlinear dose-response association between IA and depressive symptoms, while also exploring potential variations in this association across demographic subgroups.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was administered to Chinese university students. Internet addiction (IA) was assessed using an 8-item standardized diagnostic instrument. Depressive symptoms were evaluated utilizing the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression was employed to detect nonlinear relationships and identify inflection points. Multivariable logistic regression and Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel stratified analyses, controlling for potential confounders, were conducted to assess symptom-specific correlates and examine subgroup differences.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A nonlinear association was observed between IA scores and depressive symptoms ( p  < 0.005), characterized by inflection points at scores of 4 and 7. Higher odds of depressive symptoms were seen at scores exceeding 4, demonstrating a pronounced increase beyond 7, and lower odds below 4. Analysis of specific IA symptoms revealed: Preoccupation was significantly correlated with higher odds of depressive symptoms (OR = 2.60, p< 0.05); deception was associated with elevated odds of depressive symptoms (OR = 1.51, p  < 0.05); whereas needing more time online exhibited an association with lower odds of depressive symptoms (OR = 0.63, p  < 0.05). Each unit increase in IA score was associated with 31% higher overall odds of depressive symptoms (OR = 1.31, p  < 0.05). This association persisted following covariate adjustment, demonstrating a robust and independent correlational association. The positive association remained consistent across nearly all demographic and socioeconomic subgroups examined. Boarding school attendance was linked to a stronger IA-depressive-symptom association ( p  < 0.001). Furthermore, only children exhibited stronger correlational estimates between IA scores and depressive symptoms compared to non-only children (OR = 1.24, p  = 0.030).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The study indicates a positive correlational link between IA Score and depressive symptoms. RCS regression shows a curved relationship, with turning points at scores 4 and 7. Higher IA Scores correlate with elevated odds of depressive symptoms, making it a potential screening indicator for depressive-symptom risk (correlational only) for college students. Elevated odds are also present with an IA Score below 4. Excessive online activity correlates with higher odds, while prolonged internet use for gratification shows an association with lower odds of depressive symptoms.

items.title: Preliminary convergent validity and group discrimination of a serious game for assessing attention in children and adolescents with and without clinician-established ADHD.
items.authors: Ferrer-Cascales R, Costa-López B, Ruiz-Robledillo N, Albaladejo-Blázquez N, Trujillo J.

sections.text: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmentally inappropriate inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity. Diagnosis requires a comprehensive, multi-informant clinical assessment; performance on a single attention task is neither necessary nor sufficient. This cross-sectional study examined the preliminary convergent validity, reliability, and group discrimination of Attention Robots, a serious game designed to assess attention-related performance. Participants were 117 children and adolescents aged 6-18 years: 47 with a clinician-established ADHD diagnosis and 70 community comparison participants without a recorded ADHD diagnosis. Attention Robots scores were examined alongside CARAS-R and CogniFit measures using correlations, age- and sex-adjusted group comparisons, split-half reliability, and exploratory ROC analyses. Attention Robots scores were associated with CARAS-R inhibitory-control and several CogniFit measures. After adjustment for age and sex and correction for multiple comparisons, participants with ADHD showed lower Attention Robots concentration and working-speed scores than community comparison participants, whereas error percentage did not differ between groups. Among the CogniFit outcomes, only visual perception remained significantly different between groups after Holm correction. The game-only ROC model showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.61; sensitivity = 0.28; specificity = 0.80). A model that also included sex yielded an AUC of 0.73, with sensitivity of 0.57 and specificity of 0.76; however, the higher AUC cannot be attributed to the game because sex was unevenly distributed between groups. Attention Robots may provide complementary information about attention-related performance, but the present two-gate, single-site findings do not support stand-alone screening or diagnosis. Independent validation with consistently verified, sex-balanced, clinically heterogeneous samples is required.

items.title: When homophobia accumulates: cumulative association with mental health and suicidality.
items.authors: Leroy V, Sagaon Teyssier LS, Spire B, Velter A, Luiggi M.

sections.text: Existing literature often uses binary measures to investigate the link between Experienced Homophobia (EH) and mental health. However, EH may be more nuanced than binary measures can show, whilst the resulting mental health effects may vary depending on the social context in which it occurs. We aimed to estimate a context-cumulative association between EH, as manifested by acts of violences, and mental health outcomes including anxiety, psychological distress, suicidal ideations and suicide attempts. The study included 81 263 survey responses from gay men, bisexual men and other men having sex with men. We built a measure of context by violence experienced homophobia (CVEH), including verbal and physical abuse because of ones homosexuality, in multiple social contexts: workplace/educational institutions, public spaces/neighborhoods, and family. We used logistic multilevel mixed-effects model(s) to estimate the association between CVEH and the four mental health outcomes. We controlled for socioeconomic and health variables at the individual and departmental level. The more CVEH, the more the odds of being at risk of moderate/severe anxiety (aOR = 1.8 [95% CI: 1.69-1.93] to 7.1 [4.66-10.6]), psychological distress (aOR = 1.5 [1.37-1.54] to 6.4 [4.04-9.98]), suicidal ideations (aOR = 1.6 [1.46-1.70] to 4.8 [3.33-6.87]) and suicide attempts (aOR = 1.5 [1.22-1.96] to 12.5 [7.88-19.7]). Furthermore, we found that exposure to EH in workplace/educational and family contexts was more strongly associated with poorer mental health than exposure in public spaces/neighborhoods. Our findings show that EH is incrementally associated with poorer mental health, highlighting discrimination as an important social correlate of psychological distress and morbidity.

items.title: Psychosis with continuous delivery of subcutaneous levodopa: importance of the correct patient profile.
items.authors: Chaudhuri KR, Poplawska-Domaszewicz K, Bergmans B, Metta V, Odin P, Jost WH, Shalash A, van Coller R, Falup-Pecurariu C, Antonini A.

sections.text: Continuous 24-h subcutaneous infusion of foslevodopa/foscarbidopa (LDp/CDp), a soluble formulation of levodopa prodrugs delivered through a minimally invasive subcutaneous infusion system, is currently available for the management of advanced Parkinson's disease (APD) in many countries. Pivotal licensing studies and open-label studies confirm the efficacy of this first subcutaneous 24-h levodopa delivery option in APD in terms of motor effects, early-morning off periods, and sleep benefits. However, in addition to reports of skin reactions, there are also case report series and case-based concerns regarding neuropsychiatric side effects such as psychosis and hallucinations in some centres. The pattern appears to be either an early or late occurrence of psychosis, often in older patients with significant comorbidities. A critical review of such reports shows that the selected cases might have been vulnerable to psychosis, and potential corrective adjustments to the dosing of LDp/CDp were not evident; in some cases, there were unusual initiation processes. We review the entire published literature on clinical case reports of psychosis and the use of LDp/CDp and provide expert opinion-based tips on correct patient profiling and selection and on avoiding discontinuation of LDp/CDp therapy.

items.title: From ancient remedy to modern use: cannabis and cannabinoids in cancer care in the United States.
items.authors: Behl D, Abrams DI, Zylla DM, D'Andre SD.

sections.text: Cannabis, an ancient plant that has been used for millennia, is increasingly utilized by patients with cancer to alleviate symptoms related to both the disease and its treatment. This complex botanical contains multiple bioactive compounds, most notably delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD), which interact with the endogenous endocannabinoid system. THC has been studied the most, and synthetic cannabinoids are approved for the management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. However, evidence supporting cannabis for other cancer-related symptoms-including chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, insomnia, appetite stimulation, and non-neuropathic pain-remains limited. CBD alone has not demonstrated consistent or meaningful clinical benefit. Although preclinical data exist, there is no clinical evidence supporting cannabis as a cancer treatment. items.title: Understanding the role of dysfunctional hippocampal-parahippocampal representations of space in schizophrenia.
items.authors: Finger S, Kim E, Clark BJ.

sections.text: The etiology of schizophrenia is yet to be fully understood, thus limiting the scope of interventions for symptom reduction. Among features less frequently researched and addressed are deficits in spatial cognition, which may contribute to cognitive disorganization, a core symptom of schizophrenia. The purpose of this review is to summarize the known deficits in spatial memory and neural circuits associated with this neuropsychiatric disorder, synthesize key findings, and make recommendations regarding further areas of research needed in the literature. Our review identified several key areas in the brain's spatial navigation system. First, abnormal hippocampal neuronal responsivity is well-documented in patients with schizophrenia and is associated with impairments in the use of map-based strategies during navigation. Second, alterations in the synchronized firing of neurons in theta frequencies as well as the coupling of theta oscillations across cortical circuits are shown to associate with spatial problem solving. Third, recent research reports that neural representations of space, specifically relating to grid cell function, are abnormal in patients with schizophrenia and are related to deficits in navigation. We suggest that an understanding of the neural bases of behavioral and cognitive symptomology, such as cognitive disorganization, in schizophrenia will benefit from future work advancing integrated theoretical frameworks that include mechanisms of altered hippocampal-parahippocampal neuronal responses including grid cell dysfunction and altered neural oscillation patterns involved in spatial cognition.

items.title: Massive high-concentration long-acting insulin overdose with suicidal intent - a case report.
items.authors: Popiołek A, Bielun K, Niemczuk E, Pulkowski G.

sections.text: Intentional insulin overdose has been reported both in individuals with diabetes and in non-diabetic individuals who have access to insulin. As diabetology and insulin therapy continue to evolve, the pharmacodynamic profiles of insulin preparations have also changed, which may influence the clinical course of insulin overdose and poisoning. This case illustrates the prolonged metabolic consequences of a massive overdose of insulin glargine U300 in a non-diabetic individual (a total of 3,150 units administered subcutaneously). Despite its ultra-long-acting formulation, the duration of clinically significant hypoglycemia substantially exceeded that expected based on the pharmacokinetic profile, necessitating continuous intravenous glucose administration for 11 days. Throughout her hospital stay, the patient also required supplementation with phosphate, magnesium, and potassium to correct persistent electrolyte disturbances. This case highlights the importance of prolonged monitoring, aggressive glucose replacement, correction of associated electrolyte abnormalities, and multidisciplinary psychiatric management.

items.title: Technology Anxiety and Acceptance of Health Education Robots Among Patients After Abdominal Surgery: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Meng J, Feng Y, Peng L, Zhong L, Pang Q, Feng X, Zhong J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Patients differ in their willingness to accept health education robots. This study examined the association between technology anxiety and robot acceptance among patients recovering from abdominal surgery and estimated indirect associations through negative attitudes toward robots and human-robot trust.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study included 303 adults recovering from elective or emergency abdominal surgery at a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang Province, China (May-June 2026), all of whom had received at least one robot-delivered health education session. Patients with cognitive impairment, postoperative complications, or psychiatric illness were excluded. Participants completed the Robot Acceptance Questionnaire, Technophobia Scale, Negative Attitudes Toward Robots Scale, and Trust Between People and Automation Scale. PROCESS Model 6 (5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples) estimated indirect associations, specifying negative attitudes before trust a priori and adjusting for age, education, employment, income, residence, and prior robot experience. Sensitivity analyses examined the reversed ordering, HC3 standard errors, Tobit regression, and an unadjusted model.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Mean robot acceptance was 54.14 ± 10.66 (possible range, 9-63), and 18.8% of participants obtained the maximum score. Technology anxiety was negatively correlated with acceptance ( r = -0.511, p < 0.001). The standardized direct association was -0.204 (95% CI, -0.327 to -0.081). Indirect associations were -0.077 (95% CI, -0.145 to -0.012) through negative attitudes, -0.059 (95% CI, -0.111 to -0.017) through trust, and -0.014 (95% CI, -0.035 to -0.004) for the theory-ordered serial sequence. The reversed serial sequence, with trust preceding negative attitudes, was also statistically detectable (-0.012; 95% CI, -0.031 to -0.002); therefore, their ordering could not be distinguished.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Higher technology anxiety was associated with lower robot acceptance, and part of this association was statistically linked to negative attitudes and trust. Because both orderings were compatible with the cross-sectional data, these findings do not establish temporal sequence, causal mediation, or intervention effects.

items.title: The efficacy of ketogenic interventions on neuropsychological & metabolic outcomes in serious mental illness & neurocognitive disorders: a systematic review & meta-analysis.
items.authors: Maksyutynska K, Arnold C, De R, Smith EC, Panganiban KJ, Humber BE, Mak TH, Stogios N, Besa R, Andreazza AC, Ebdrup BH, Zemmour K, Cunnane SC, Agarwal SM, Hahn MK.

sections.text: Ketogenic interventions have garnered attention for their potential benefits in individuals with psychiatric and neurocognitive disorders. This review analyzed findings from studies investigating the impact of ketogenic interventions on clinical outcomes in individuals with serious mental illness (SMI) and neurocognitive disorders. A comprehensive search was conducted to identify studies reporting on psychopathology or cognitive performance in individuals with schizophrenia spectrum, major mood, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or major neurocognitive disorders/dementia treated with a ketogenic intervention. Changes in body composition, metabolic parameters, adherence, and safety were also assessed. Evidence was organized by population and outcome of interest, and supplemented by a quantitative meta-analysis. Seventy-three studies (SMI k = 31; neurocognitive disorders k = 42) were included, with treatment durations ranging from single-dose interventions up to 12 years. Evidence in SMI was largely limited to case reports and single-arm trials reporting symptom remission, reductions in positive and negative symptoms, and mood improvements. Controlled trials in neurocognitive disorders provided more substantiated evidence amenable to meta-analysis. Ketogenic interventions improved cognitive performance (SMD 0.24, 95% CI [0.06, 0.43], p = 0.01, n = 587, k = 14, I² = 61%) and reduced body weight (MD - 3.13 kg, 95% CI [-5.91, -0.35], p = 0.03, n = 80, k = 3, I² = 6%) in this population. Gastrointestinal symptoms were the most frequently reported adverse event. While the evidence for ketogenic interventions differs by population, promising findings emerge. In neurocognitive disorders, controlled trial data support modest cognitive and metabolic benefits. In SMI, preliminary evidence highlights the evolving nature of this field and the need for more rigorous investigation, including RCTs, to establish clinical safety and efficacy.

items.title: Effects of physical activity-centered programs on mental health in adolescents experiencing social disadvantage: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
items.authors: Fang T, Li H.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Social disadvantage can increase adolescents' exposure to stress while limiting support and access to care. Physical activity programs fit everyday settings, but their effects and transferability remain uncertain. We assessed physical activity-centered programs for adolescents aged 10-19 years experiencing verifiable social disadvantage.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched seven databases through 1 September 2026, rerunning all seven on 8 September. Randomized and non-randomized controlled interventions were eligible. Two reviewers conducted screening, data verification, and evidence assessment. The study family was the independent weighting unit and the specific psychological construct was the synthesis unit. Comparable constructs represented by at least two families were synthesized using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp inference. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, cluster RoB 2, or ROBINS-I, and three important outcomes were evaluated with GRADE.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Fourteen reports from 12 study families from 8 countries were included; 8 families were randomized, including 4 cluster trials. In randomized no-added-program comparisons, immediate depression could be pooled across only two families, with estimates pointing in opposite directions ( g  = -0.256, 95% CI [-5.442, 4.930]; I ^2 = 91.8%; very low certainty). General anxiety was represented by one randomized family; the estimate favored the wait-list ( g  = -0.627, 95% CI [-0.955, -0.298]; low certainty). One four-school trial found a positive impact on wellbeing; however, the estimate was uncertain ( g  = 0.220; df  = 2; interval [-0.505, 0.944]; very low certainty). Other findings were largely family-specific, and safety reporting was incomplete.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Sparse, heterogeneous evidence does not establish mental health effects generalizable across socially disadvantaged adolescents. The roles of program content, comparators, and social context remain unresolved. Physical activity-centered programs should be evaluated further within existing care and social support, with a focus on implementation, psychosocial resources, and possible risks.

items.title: Enhancing psychological wellbeing in STEM education through public health strategies across educational transitions.
items.authors: Zhang L, Zhang Z, Qu J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Student mental health is a growing public health concern in higher education, and small questionnaire datasets are often highly imbalanced and difficult to model reliably.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This study empirically validates a Transition-Aware Public Health Wellbeing Network (TAPHW-Net) using an openly accessible questionnaire dataset and narrows the STEM-transition domain to the available variables.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The source dataset contained 843 responses. Respondents aged 18-22 years were retained, and the analytic sample consisted of 777 students, classified based on the original survey label: No Stress ( n  = 38), Eustress ( n  = 710), and Distress ( n  = 29). 24 predictors were grouped into emotional/psychological, physical/somatic, academic pressure, social and environmental, and demographic branches. To prevent leakage of the targets, the direct recent-stress item was omitted. Median imputation, standardization, and SMOTE were applied in the training folds only. Five-fold out-of-fold evaluation was used to assess Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, MLP, ANN, and TAPHW-Net.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Logistic Regression had the highest fold-averaged accuracy (0.968 ± 0.019), macro-F1 (0.884 ± 0.048), and macro-AUC (0.996 ± 0.004). TAPHW-Net's pooled OOF accuracy, macro-F1 score, and macro-AUC were 0.8739, 0.6626, and 0.9523, respectively. It had lower overall accuracy, but it successfully retrieved 78.9% of the No Stress cases and 86.2% of the distress cases, although precision was only 0.385 and 0.397 for these two classes, respectively. Difficulty in the home environment, anxiety, palpitations, work-environment stress, sleep problems, and health problems were important predictors.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The attention architecture did not outperform simpler models on this small and highly imbalanced tabular dataset. Its main value lies in domain-structured representations, minority-class recall, and transparent mapping of model importance to a hypothetical decision-support template. The findings are limited to the source dataset and require external validation before institutional use or transfer to STEM-specific and educational-transition settings.

items.title: Metformin in Metabolic Psychiatry from Cellular Bioenergetics to Brain Network Homeostasis: A Narrative Review.
items.authors: Ma J, Chen J, Cao T, Zhong BL.

sections.text: Metabolic psychiatry links severe mental illness to impaired brain and systemic energy metabolism, yet few treatments directly target this pathway. Metformin is widely prescribed to limit antipsychotic (AP)-induced weight gain, but growing evidence suggests it also influences central nervous system function. This narrative review organizes findings from cellular, animal, and human studies into a three-step model connecting cellular bioenergetics to brain network (BN) homeostasis. This proposed central cascade rests almost entirely on rodent and cellular studies, where metformin activates neuronal AMP-activated protein kinase, modulates gene regulation, and dampens microglial inflammation to support synaptic plasticity. In clinical trials, starting metformin alongside antipsychotics (APs) reliably reduces weight gain and insulin resistance (IR). A small number of preliminary clinical trials in schizophrenia and bipolar depression also report improved prefrontal-hippocampal connectivity or mood symptom relief, with psychiatric gains occurring mainly in patients whose peripheral IR resolves. Because metformin crosses the human blood-brain barrier in limited amounts and direct human evidence for its central mechanisms remains scarce, future randomized trials should use metabolic biomarkers to identify the patient subgroups most likely to benefit.

items.title: Ritualization of euthanasia in cases of unbearable psychiatric versus unbearable somatic suffering in the Netherlands: a comparison.
items.authors: Ceelen I, Strijbos D, Jedan C, de Kort H, Venbrux E.

sections.text: The Netherlands has an established euthanasia practice. The increase in euthanasia cases for psychiatric suffering over the past 10 years is subject to ongoing public and political debate. During the fieldwork of the research project "ritualisation of euthanasia", remarkable differences between euthanasia cases for somatic suffering and psychiatric suffering were observed, which sparked a closer investigation. This article analyses how euthanasia is ritualised differently in cases of those two groups and tentatively explained using theories from ritual studies, sociology and anthropology. Between November 2023 and November 2025, 52 euthanasia cases were explored using a multi-sited focused ethnography approach. Through observations and prospective and retrospective interviews, data was collected and analysed using constant comparative methods. This paper reveals that psychiatric cases, often younger people and more socially stigmatised, engage in more expressive, symbolic, and creative rituals, such as curated funerals, memory boxes, and tattoos. In contrast, somatic cases tend to focus on relational closure through familiar and everyday rituals. The paper highlights how ritual behaviour reflects age, stigma, and social positioning, with rituals in psychiatric cases serving the creation of a post-self, recognition, agency, and active narrative shaping at the end of life. The findings suggest that ritualisation is not only personal but also deeply socio-cultural and moral, offering insight into how different forms of suffering shape the meaning of a "good death".

items.title: Ketamine promotes strategic and efficient approach-avoidance conflict resolution.
items.authors: Vestring S, Pfauth S, Galuba V, Burgos Kim G, Bach DR, Mülsch F, Mocayar Marón F, Domschke K, Endres D, Normann C, Baldermann JC.

sections.text: Adaptive behavior requires flexibly balancing approach and avoidance in risky or threatening environments, a flexibility disrupted in depression and other disorders marked by excessive avoidance. Benzodiazepines such as lorazepam broadly dampen neural excitability and synaptic plasticity, whereas ketamine may enhance both. We therefore asked whether ketamine promotes more strategic and efficient motivational behavior. In this completed randomized crossover study, 34 healthy participants with no lifetime neurological or psychiatric disorders and no regular medication use were assessed at the University Medical Center Freiburg (DRKS00025471). Participants completed three visits separated by seven days: a control visit without medication, followed by intranasal ketamine (50 mg) and oral lorazepam (1 mg) in randomized, counterbalanced order. Threat probability and loss magnitude were varied independently in a dynamic approach-avoidance conflict task conducted after ketamine's acute dissociative phase. Reported behavioral outcomes were net token gain, approach behavior, and approach and withdrawal latencies. Behavioral assessors were blinded to condition; participants and physicians were not. Mixed-effects models were used. All 34 randomized participants completed each condition and were analyzed. Ketamine yielded 57% higher token gains than control (β = 0.09, 95% confidence interval 0.05 to 0.13; p < 0.001) and 33% higher gains than lorazepam (β = 0.05, 0.01 to 0.09; p = 0.009). Behavior following ketamine was more strongly guided by outcome value than threat probability and showed faster approach and withdrawal responses. items.title: The Role of Family Social Capital in Recovery From Mental Health Challenges: A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Kellenaers F, Heesen K, Duel J, van Ee E.

sections.text: Current mental health care primarily focuses on patients, even though mental health problems may affect entire families. Involving family members in treatment could foster a more sustainable recovery. Although family members are a key part of a patient's social capital, which includes the resources within the patient's social network, family members also have their own network they can draw upon. Family social capital could potentially function as a powerful catalyser in recovery from mental health problems by one of the family members, but little is known about these mechanisms. This review aims to investigate how family social capital is operationalized in mental health care studies, gather existing knowledge on the role of family social capital in mental health recovery by one of the family members, investigate the impact of mental health interventions on family social capital, and identify remaining research gaps. We systematically searched scientific databases, selected and charted 25 studies (1984-2024) that measured social capital in patients in need of mental health care and their families. Most studies measured only narrow aspects of family social capital. We summarized the association between social capital and recovery in four themes: (a) Size of the network; (b) perceived social support; (c) social involvement versus social isolation; and (d) perceived barriers in accessing family social capital. The findings illustrate how vital it is to involve family and the social network in both treatment and research. A greater emphasis on the social context is needed in both research and clinical practice.

items.title: A Rare Case of Fulminant Guillain-Barre Syndrome as the Cardinal Presenting Feature of New Onset Pediatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.authors: Coss S, Poisson KE, Driest K, Leib S, Wilson C, Sunderland E, Harvey-Nuckles K, Lamberta LK.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Here we present a complex case of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presenting initially as fulminant Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS). This particular manifestation of neuropsychiatric lupus is uncommon but can be severe and even life threatening. Increasing providers' awareness of the overlap between lupus and GBS will improve diagnostic accuracy and timing as well as expedite appropriate therapies, which may differ from typical GBS treatment.

sections.heading: Case presentation
sections.text: A 12-year-old previously healthy Hispanic female presented with subacute onset vision changes and imbalance with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and hyporeflexia. Given her classic clinical triad and suspicion for GBS variant Miller Fischer syndrome (MFS), neuroaxis imaging was obtained. MRI showed cranial nerve and ventral nerve root enhancement, and cytoalbuminologic dissociation seen on cerebrospinal fluid analysis also supported this diagnosis. Weakness including the facial and bulbar muscles and the extremities progressed rapidly and threatened respiratory functions, so the patient was intubated. Typical treatments for GBS including intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and plasma exchange (PLEX) were insufficient to manage symptoms, and additional evaluations supported a diagnosis of SLE with nephritis. Coordinated care between neuroimmunology and rheumatology enabled rapid escalation of therapy to include high-dose intravenous steroid pulses, cyclophosphamide, and rituximab. Together, these therapies eventually stabilized the patient, and with support from neuropsychology, psychiatry, and rehabilitation medicine, she was able to discharge from the hospital after 115 days of admission. She has remained in remission on maintenance immunosuppression including mycophenolate mofetil as well as hydroxychloroquine.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Neuropsychiatric lupus can be difficult to diagnose and manage, but its severity necessitates vigilance and aggressive management. In the current case, the isolated neurological symptoms at presentation consistent with GBS could have delayed diagnosis, but neuroimmunology and rheumatology were consulted early, and appropriate diagnostic testing was performed. The patient's multidisciplinary team worked closely together to appropriately escalate her treatment beyond what is typical for GBS, ultimately leading to remission of her neuropsychiatric symptoms and recovery of her baseline neurological status. This case highlights the complex nature of neuropsychiatric lupus, suggests that SLE should be on the differential in atypical or difficult-to-treat cases of GBS, and underscores the need for coordinated interdisciplinary care to achieve best outcomes for these patients.

items.title: The Increasing Predominance of Emergency Hospitalizations for Neurotic and Stress-Related Disorders in Brazil (2015-2024).
items.authors: Dos Santos Terceiro LL, Da Rocha Sady LM, Rodrigues Alves MFS, Marques Filho FCB, Clementino VA, Araújo LN, Bernardi TC, Ananias LF.

sections.text: Objective  Neurotic, stress-related, and somatoform disorders are important contributors to psychiatric morbidity and healthcare utilisation. This study aimed to characterise the epidemiological profile and temporal trends of hospitalisations for neurotic, stress-related, and somatoform disorders in Brazil between 2015 and 2024. Methods  This retrospective ecological time-series study analysed hospitalisations recorded in the Brazilian Unified Health System for which the primary diagnosis corresponded to ICD-10 codes F40-F48. Data were stratified by sex, age group, geographic region, and type of admission. Temporal trends were assessed using linear regression, and group differences were evaluated using non-parametric tests, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results A total of 29,908 hospitalisations were recorded during the study period. The annual number of hospitalisations increased by 94.0%, from 2,263 cases in 2015 to 4,391 cases in 2024. Emergency admissions accounted for 84.7% (n = 25,332) of all hospitalisations and increased by 151.7%, from 1,574 cases in 2015 to 3,962 cases in 2024, whereas elective admissions decreased by 37.7%. Overall hospitalisations showed a significant upward temporal trend (β = 203.2 admissions/year; R² = 0.689; p = 0.003). The most pronounced increases were observed among females (β = 168.9 admissions/year; p < 0.001) and individuals aged 20-29 years (β = 54.3 admissions/year; p = 0.002), with significant upward trends also observed in most geographic regions (p < 0.01). Conclusions Hospitalisations for neurotic, stress-related, and somatoform disorders increased substantially in Brazil between 2015 and 2024, primarily driven by the marked rise in emergency admissions, particularly among females and young adults. These findings highlight the need to strengthen outpatient and community-based mental healthcare, improve early identification and management of these disorders, and reduce potentially avoidable reliance on hospital-based and crisis-oriented care.

items.title: Kundalini phenomenology as expansion of perceptual capacity: a hypothesis and theory article integrating contemplative traditions and neuroscience.
items.authors: Samanta S.

sections.text: Kundalini experiences-characterised by sensations of internal energy movement, sequential anatomical progression, boundary dissolution, and reports of expanded or cosmic consciousness-have been documented across contemplative traditions for millennia, yet remain theoretically underspecified within contemporary neuroscience. This paper proposes that these experiences can be understood, without metaphysical commitment, as reflecting a state-dependent expansion of perceptual capacity: the range and dimensionality across which an organism can apprehend patterns of integration, continuity, and coherence. The framework draws a distinction between perceptual capacity (what can be perceived) and perceptual content (what happens to be perceived at any moment), and argues that kundalini phenomenology maps onto progressive shifts from narrow, body-local, temporally fragmented perception toward multidimensional integrative awareness. The proposal is situated within three converging neuroscientific frameworks-global neuronal workspace theory, predictive processing, and network integration approaches-and is tested for structural consistency against liberation phenomenology across seven contemplative traditions: Śaiva/Tantric Hinduism, Pātañjala Yoga, Advaita Vedānta, Theravāda and Tibetan Buddhism, Daoism (neidan), Sufism (fanā/baqā), and Greek Stoicism. Where these traditions converge in describing a shift from positionally fixed to non-positionally witnessing consciousness, despite operating within substantially different cosmological and linguistic frameworks, the convergence constitutes evidence-not proof, but evidence-that a common phenomenological structure is being independently observed. The framework generates five falsifiable predictions, each specifying the measure, population, and expected direction of effect. It proposes that safety versus crisis outcomes in contemplative practice depend critically on the rate of perceptual expansion relative to individual integration capacity, and offers provisional clinical heuristics-explicitly labelled as hypotheses requiring prospective validation-for differential diagnosis between contemplative states and psychotic episodes. The present paper extends and complements the author's previously published neurophysiological model of kundalini, which proposed biomarker-level correspondences and a composite tracking metric (NDI); the present contribution addresses the phenomenological and perceptual-theoretic dimension that the earlier paper did not develop.

items.title: Public mental health implications of intelligent heritage environments for wellbeing: environmental-psychological pathways across SDG 3 and SDG 11.
items.authors: Feng S, Huang W, Ao J, Li W, Wang Y.

sections.text: Heritage environments combine architectural space, cultural participation, and digital mediation, yet evidence on their environmental-psychological and public-health implications remains fragmented. This review pursued two linked objectives: to map the literature across time, geography, themes, methods, and environmental configurations, and to identify recurrent pathways linking environmental conditions to psychological mechanisms and wellbeing outcomes. We screened Web of Science and Scopus records published from 2015 to 2025 using a PRISMA-guided procedure. The final corpus comprised 253 publications analyzed through scientometric mapping, full-text content coding, citation-neighborhood tracing, and independent reliability assessment. Objective 1 showed that publication growth accelerated after 2023, with output shifting toward Asia while cumulative citation influence remained concentrated in earlier European work. Keyword networks retained a person-environment core while differentiating environmental-perception, health, immersive, and computational themes. Content coding distinguished actual socio-physical heritage settings, virtual counterparts, hybrid technology-augmented settings, and transferable environmental-psychology evidence. Objective 2 identified recurrent pathways linking these configurations with affect/restoration, perception/cognition, place attachment, presence/embodiment, social participation, and restorative, affective, social, cognitive, and accessibility-related wellbeing outcomes. Policy evidence was concentrated in SDG 11 and integrated SDG 3-SDG 11 relevance. Intelligent heritage environments emerge as an environmental-psychology problem in which spatial conditions, cultural meaning, and digital mediation interact. The evidence-traceable framework is conceptual and is intended to guide hypothesis development, measurement, and comparative testing rather than serve as a validated causal, clinical, or policy-effectiveness model. Future tests should extend across diverse heritage contexts.
