items.title: The relationship between Tai Chi exercise and psychological distress in older adults: the chain mediation effect of mood state and sleep quality.
items.authors: Xu P, Yang L.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Psychological distress is a common mental health issue among older adults, significantly affecting their quality of life and overall health. As a traditional form of mind-body exercise, Tai Chi is gaining increasing attention for its mental health benefits. However, the effects of Tai Chi practice on psychological distress in older adults remain unclear, and the mechanisms underlying its impact on mood and sleep quality, in particular, still need to be explored.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This study aims to explore the relationship between Tai Chi exercise and psychological distress in older adults, and to examine the chained mediating effects of mood state and sleep quality in this association.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.text: Questionnaires containing the Physical Activity Rating Scale (PARS-3), the Positive and Negative Mood States (POMS) scale, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQ), and the final versions of non-specific psychological distress scales (Kessler 10), a total of 457 valid questionnaires were collected.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Analysis of the mediation effects in this study were statistically consistent with a mediating role of the relationship between Tai Chi exercise and psychological distress in older adults. The effect size of the total indirect effect was -0.265 (95% CI [-0.339, -0.197], p  < 0.01), accounting for 53.9% of the total effect. The mediation effect consisted of three pathways. Path 1: Tai Chi exercise → Mood state → Psychological distress in older adults, with an effect size of -0.159 (95% CI [-0.221, -0.103], p  < 0.01). Path 2: Tai Chi exercise → Sleep quality → Psychological distress in older adults, with an effect size of -0.067 (95% CI [-0.112, -0.032], p  < 0.01). Path 3: Tai Chi exercise → Mood state → Sleep quality → Psychological distress in older adults, with an effect size of -0.039 (95% CI [-0.065, -0.020], p  < 0.01).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study identified a significant association between Tai Chi exercise and the alleviation of psychological distress in older adults, and this association may be explained by the chained mediating effects of mood state and sleep quality.

items.title: Racial Disparities in Postpartum Morbidity and Mortality: A Systematic Review of Structural and Healthcare Systems Factors With AI/ML Applications.
items.authors: Baba D, Mmamelu P.
items.journal: International journal of MCH and AIDS

sections.heading: Background and objective
sections.text: Racial disparities in maternal and postpartum health remain substantial in the United States. In 2024, the maternal mortality rate among non-Hispanic Black women was 44.8 deaths per 100,000 live births, compared with 14.2 among non-Hispanic White women. This systematic review synthesized contemporary evidence on racial disparities in postpartum morbidity and mortality, contributing structural and healthcare factors, emerging artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications, and interventions intended to improve postpartum outcomes and equity.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. The evidence synthesis focused on U.S.-based primary empirical studies and authoritative government surveillance and analytic sources addressing maternal and postpartum outcomes, racial and ethnic disparities, structural and social determinants of health, healthcare access, artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications, and interventions relevant to postpartum health. We used systematic and scoping reviews for citation identification and contextual interpretation but did not count them as independent primary evidence. Because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, exposures, and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The evidence demonstrated persistent racial and ethnic disparities across maternal mortality, severe maternal morbidity and postpartum hemorrhage, peripartum cardiomyopathy and hypertensive disorders, postpartum mental health, and access to postpartum care. In 2024, non-Hispanic Black women experienced a maternal mortality rate approximately 3.2 times that of non-Hispanic White women. Pregnancy-related mortality surveillance further showed that a substantial proportion of deaths occurred beyond 42 days after pregnancy, underscoring the importance of care throughout the first postpartum year. Machine-learning studies demonstrated promising discrimination for selected maternal morbidity outcomes, but evidence regarding external validation, equitable performance across demographic subgroups, and prospective clinical implementation remained limited. Evidence on interventions was strongest for standardized obstetric quality-improvement initiatives, while postpartum Medicaid extensions, doula care, and paid family leave showed benefits in selected access, utilization, or patient-centered outcomes but did not consistently demonstrate reductions in racial disparities in severe morbidity or mortality.

sections.heading: Conclusions and global health implications
sections.text: Persistent racial disparities in U.S. maternal and postpartum health likely reflect intersecting clinical, healthcare-system, socioeconomic, and structural factors. Reducing these inequities requires sustained postpartum surveillance and care, rigorous evaluation of interventions, attention to structural determinants, culturally responsive mental-health services, and transparent validation of emerging predictive technologies across diverse populations.

items.authors: Henderson J, Furlong A.

items.title: Subjective Mental Health and Oral Health of Korean Adolescents.
items.authors: Son HK, Sim E.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: This study aimed to assess the status of subjective oral health and mental health among Korean adolescents using data from the 2024 Korea Youth Risk Behavior Web-based Survey (KYRBS), and to examine the independent associations between mental health indicators and oral symptom experiences.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were analyzed from the 20th KYRBS, comprising 54,653 adolescents. Subjective oral symptoms were categorized as: (I) tooth pain when consuming hot or cold food/beverages, (II) throbbing or aching tooth pain, and (III) gum pain or bleeding. Mental health variables included perceived stress, feelings of sadness or despair, and loneliness. All analyses accounted for the complex sampling design (weights, stratification, and clustering).

items.title: Diquat Poisoning: Epidemiology, Molecular Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Clinical Management.
items.authors: Qian W, Tang S, Liu B, Xie X, Peng A, Cao Y.

sections.text: Diquat (1,1'-ethylene-2,2'-bipyridinium dibromide) is a nonselective bipyridyl herbicide widely used in agriculture for crop desiccation and weed control. Following the global restriction of paraquat, diquat usage has surged substantially, leading to increased poisoning incidents particularly in agricultural regions of China and other developing countries, where intentional ingestion for self-harm constitutes the predominant exposure route with mortality rates of 16.7-60% depending on ingested dose and treatment timing. At the molecular level, diquat undergoes nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH)-dependent redox cycling generating excessive reactive oxygen species, triggering mitochondrial dysfunction, Nrf2-Keap1 pathway activation, and multiple regulated cell death modalities including apoptosis, necroptosis, and ferroptosis. However, a comprehensive synthesis integrating epidemiological patterns, molecular mechanisms, organ-specific pathophysiology, and evidence-based clinical management remains lacking. This review systematically examines the global epidemiology and demographic characteristics of diquat poisoning, elucidates the interconnected molecular pathways underlying multiorgan toxicity affecting kidneys, liver, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system, evaluates current diagnostic approaches including severity scoring systems and biomarker-guided prognostication, and critically appraises therapeutic strategies from emergency decontamination to investigational cell death pathway inhibitors. This work provides a comprehensive framework for understanding diquat toxicology and identifies critical knowledge gaps to guide future research toward precision medicine approaches and improved clinical outcomes.

items.title: Organising, sustaining, experiencing and integrating mental health crisis care for children and young people: qualitative findings from eight contrasting case studies in England and Wales.
items.authors: Bennett C, Williams J, Sawle L, Fraser C, Vaughan R, Pryjmachuk S, McMillan I, Jones A, Hails E, Bennett N, Elliott M, Elliott M, Hannigan B.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Crisis services are an important part of the system of mental health care for children and young people (CYP), but little is known about them or the experiences of CYP and families. This article reports findings from a normalisation process theory (NPT)-informed sequential mixed methods study, comprising three work packages (WPs), which set out to generate new knowledge in this area.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Approaches to CYP crisis care across England and Wales were mapped in WP1 using survey design. Previously reported findings from this WP point to heterogeneity in service types and interventions. In WP2 eight contrasting services (five in England, three in Wales) were selected from WP1 survey returns as case studies. In each case, interviews were held with CYP, parents/carers, commissioners, managers, practitioners and others. Within-case data were analysed using both NPT-informed framework, and inductive, approaches. In WP3 a cross-case synthesis led to the identification of key principles for future policy, services and practice.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 137 people took part in interviews (25 CYP, 25 parents/carers, 45 practitioners, 28 managers, seven commissioners and seven local stakeholders). Each service's planned, deliberative, approach to crisis care implementation for CYP revealed strategic intentions, but variation was found in aims, goals and experiences. Differences were found in local capacities to adapt, negotiate and reframe available resources. Significant variation existed in the coherence of the crisis care offer, and with how individuals and groups worked alone and together to participate in implementation. Likewise, diversity was revealed in the effects crisis services exerted within their local systems.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Key principles underpinning the whole-system provision of sustainable mental health crisis care for CYP include: accessibility; the need for support in navigating complex systems; clarity on the offer; staff expertise and interpersonal skills; targeted services; continuity; flexibility balanced with stability; and service integration.

items.title: Recreational opportunities and mentorship at Play Marin enhance health and well-being for adolescents in Marin City, CA.
items.authors: George MF, Snyder RA, Angelonides SC, Leon KM, Rios De Leon SB, Austin P, Ereman RR.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: Finding evidence-based interventions and community supported solutions to the mental health crisis among youth is imperative. We aimed to understand the impact of Play Marin (PM, a community-based organization) on overall well-being using data collected from current and former students and community members.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The research methodology consisted of a mixed methods approach: interviews were conducted with students of PM, family members and coaches in the Spring of 2024. Quantitatively, the survey data were compared between former students of PM and the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS), collected in 2024.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Qualitatively revealed results that individuals associated with PM experienced recreational opportunities and mentorship, better mental and physical health, and increased feelings of belonging. Quantitative results suggested participants had better mental health, less screentime, competed on more sports teams, slept more on school nights, vaped less, and felt closer to other students at school ( p  < 0.05) as compared to the YRBSS.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The current mental health crisis may be alleviated with increased recreational opportunities and mentorship for adolescents and young adults through community engagement and positive interactions. Exposure to mentors with lived experiences help adolescents gain necessary tools and resources to make better health decisions than the YRBSS.

items.title: When therapy meets the bench: subpoenaed clinical notes in family law.
items.authors: Dodds L, Moritz D, Creamer C.
items.journal: Psychiatry, psychology, and law : an interdisciplinary journal of the Australian and New Zealand Association of Psychiatry, Psychology and Law

sections.text: This study presents the first systematic examination of mental health practitioners' experiences with the subpoenaing of clinical notes and their use by family report writers in Australian family law proceedings. The findings reveal that current subpoena practices can significantly undermine therapeutic relationships and compromise the emotional and psychological safety of clients, particularly children and parents involved in parenting disputes. These risks are further amplified when clients are victim-survivors of family violence. Mental health professionals and family report writers share concerns about the broader implications of this practice, including the erosion of trust in therapeutic settings and the limited relevance of clinical notes for legal decision-making. The study underscores the urgent need to distinguish between practices that genuinely support the rights and wellbeing of families, and those that risk causing unintended harm. It calls for critical scrutiny of compelled disclosure to ensure legal processes align with child-centred, trauma-informed and rights-based approaches to decision-making.

items.title: Mental health in context: Applying a lifecourse perspective to understanding mental health, work and welfare.
items.authors: Irvine A.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: With rising rates of reported mental ill health being reflected in trends in benefit receipt, a policy narrative has taken hold that mental health problems are driving the UK's recent increase in economic inactivity. However, while these quantitative trends reflect real experiences of distress, the dominance of mental health as a statistical and administrative explanation for economic inactivity masks significant complexity in the reasons why people are unable to seek, find or sustain employment. Taking a holistic lifecourse perspective on mental health and employment, this study aimed to illuminate the ways in which biography, mental health and social structures are interwoven in ways which challenge deterministic, medicalised and individualised explanations of economic inactivity.

sections.heading: Study design
sections.text: Qualitative longitudinal and biographical narrative methods.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Biographical interviews with 23 individuals who had experience of both paid employment and the UK benefits system, and who self-identified as having experience of mental health problems. Two longitudinal follow-up interviews over 12-18 months to capture continuity and change in the contemporary policy context.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Participants represented a diverse range of educational, employment and wider biographical circumstances. However, recurring themes included adverse childhood experiences, derailed education, caring responsibilities, violence and abuse. All of these directly shaped and constrained people's employment prospects and pathways, as well as impacting their mental health. Difficulties securing a stable foothold in the world of work, due to these accumulated disadvantages, left many participants vulnerable to precarious and insecure work.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Whilst direct support for mental health remains vital, policies aimed at reducing economic inactivity need to take a much wider view, addressing the multitude of intersecting obstacles faced by people with mental health problems. For public health specialists, there is a vested interest in systems-based and cross-sector collaboration across the spectrum of public services, given the associations between good quality work and positive health outcomes.

items.title: Quality of life and musculoskeletal function among small-scale fishers in Yucatán, Mexico: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Martínez-García D, Cueva-G Cantón A, Huchim-Lara O, García Naranjo-Urzaiz AT.
items.journal: Revista brasileira de medicina do trabalho : publicacao oficial da Associacao Nacional de Medicina do Trabalho-ANAMT

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Small-scale fishers face occupational hazards and physical demands that may affect musculoskeletal health and quality of life.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To assess health-related quality of life, low-back disability, and upper-limb disability among small-scale fishers from two coastal communities in Yucatán, Mexico.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study included a convenience sample of 55 artisanal fishers. Health-related quality of life, low-back disability, and upper-limb disability were assessed using SF-36, Oswestry Disability Index, and QuickDASH, respectively. Shoulder range of motion and handgrip strength were also measured. Descriptive analyses and exploratory comparisons (by community and by diving status) were performed.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Median age was 33 years; 94.5% were men. The lowest SF-36 scores occurred in the role-physical (50), general-health-perception (62), and role-emotional (66.6) domains, whereas social functioning scored highest (87.5). Among 17 participants reporting low-back pain, 14 (82.4%) had minimal disability. The median QuickDASH score was 11.4. Mental health scores were higher in Rio Lagartos than in San Felipe (88 vs. 72; p=0.042); other SF-36 domains did not differ by community. No significant differences in SF-36 domains or QuickDASH scores were detected by diving status, although only seven participants were non-divers. Among divers, SF-36 domain scores did not differ significantly by self-reported episodes consistent with decompression sickness.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The lowest median SF-36 scores were observed in physical and emotional role limitations and general health perceptions, whereas social functioning had the highest median score. Low-back disability was predominantly minimal, and upper-limb disability was low. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger, representative studies.

items.title: The psychosocial resilience experiences of healthcare workers following the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes: a qualitative study.
items.authors: Şimşek BB, Şahin H, Yıldız İ, Ekşi A.

sections.text: This study explores the under-researched experiences of healthcare workers navigating a "dual-role" paradox, functioning simultaneously as traumatised disaster survivors and active responders during the 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes. Disasters fracture a community's social fabric, highlighting the need to understand the dynamic interactions that shape the adaptive capacities of frontline healthcare workers in disrupted environments. Moving beyond individual-centric approaches, this research provides a socio-ecological framework demonstrating that resilience is a multidimensional outcome, offering critical insights for post-disaster mental health strategies. To investigate the psychosocial resilience and resource mobilisation of these professionals across individual, interpersonal, and organisational levels, a qualitative approach was employed. In-depth interviews were conducted with 33 frontline healthcare workers (paramedics/ emergency medical technicians [EMTs], nurses, emergency physicians, and psychosocial staff) active in the immediate aftermath. Data were evaluated via thematic analysis and interpreted through the Socio-Ecological Model (SEM). The sample (mean age: 32.00 ± 5.33) primarily comprised pre-hospital emergency personnel (n = 16, 48.5%). Highlighting the extreme demands of their position, all participants worked continuously for over 72 h acutely, despite their own homes sustaining mild damage. The thematic analysis identified three main themes: Psychological Resilience, Social and Communal Support, and Organisational and Occupational Challenges. Healthcare workers experienced severe occupational role conflict, ethical distress, and security vulnerabilities. Despite the psychological toll, participants exhibited psychological flexibility and a heightened awareness of life's fragility. Family bonds, collegial solidarity, and community support emerged as essential support systems. Integrating the SEM with the dual-role framework of healthcare workers, this study reinforces that disaster resilience is a socially and organisationally embedded process shaped by complex interactions. Shifting from traditional individual paradigms, these findings offer policymakers and crisis managers strategic guidance on developing multi-layered support systems that address the unique role conflicts faced by healthcare workers in future disasters.

items.title: Staff and Pupil Perceptions of Factors Influencing School Connectedness in Wales and Implications for Emotional and Mental Wellbeing Policy.
items.authors: Brown R, Anthony R, Donaldson C, Edwards A, Haslam Z, Kolosowska A, Lennon J, Moore G.

sections.text: School connectedness broadly refers to the sense of belonging and attachment that pupils feel towards their school community. Exploring school connectedness supports understanding of how features of the school community affect the mental health and wellbeing of pupils within the school. As part of a wider evaluation of the Welsh Government Framework on Embedding a Whole School Approach to Emotional and Mental Wellbeing, data was collected through qualitative group interviews with staff and pupils at twelve case study schools in Wales. These explored factors related to school connectedness, including relationships with staff and other pupils, opportunities for involvement in school life, relationships and stressors within schools and school actions aimed at maintaining a cohesive community. Findings presented here discuss barriers and facilitators to developing and maintaining school connectedness in the context of the Covid-19 pandemic and in response to Welsh Government policy. The paper describes challenges faced by schools, including increases in complex developmental and behavioural needs after the pandemic, the challenge of maintaining connectivity in light of absence rates and staff capacity and workload. It also presents staff and pupils views of some of the school-level activities in operation and discussed implications for current policy. This paper can support policy-makers and educationalists in understanding key contextual challenges likely to impact implementation of the Framework on Embedding a Whole School Approach to Emotional and Mental Wellbeing. It also highlights challenges in attributing observed changes solely to the Framework.

items.title: Predictive modeling of sleep quality during health crises: a primary dataset from COVID-19 among Bangladeshi population.
items.authors: Quais I, Fairooz QF, Tasnim H, Begum A, Hossain S, Mahmud I.

sections.text: The COVID-19 pandemic had a significant impact on sleep health globally, and developing nations like Bangladesh has added complexity due to population density, socio-economic issues, and a lack of mental health resources. This article shares a primary dataset from 945 respondents (59.2% male, 40.8% female) in Bangladesh for use in research studies on sleep health during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The dataset includes socio-demographic and socioeconomic variables, lifestyle, behavioral and COVID-19 related variables, and sleep and insomnia related variables, such as Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) responses. The data was gathered by using a structured questionnaire, and then preprocessed using cleaning, encoding, and validation procedures to ensure consistency and usability of the data. To describe the study population and structure of the data set descriptive statistics are applied. This freely accessible data may be useful for future research in public health, sleep medicine, epidemiology, behavioral science, mental health, and for data-driven studies of sleep-related outcomes in the Global South.

items.authors: Clemente-Sánchez M, Garcia-Molina I, Rodríguez-Zafra A, Aostri E, Nazabal A.

sections.heading: Introduction

items.title: Competition pressure and psychological resilience among university teachers: a mixed-methods study of teaching competitions in Chinese higher education.
items.authors: Chen J, Sui D, Yu Y, Zhang M.

sections.text: Teaching competitions are an important way to enhance teachers' teaching abilities. However, the traditional management model of school competitions generally has a tendency of "emphasizing skills over mental effort," with a single evaluation dimension and a lack of systematic attention to teachers' mental health and psychological resilience. This study focuses on the model innovation of "Mental Education Empowerment Dual-track Drive," and builds a institution-level (school-level) competition management paradigm for the collaborative evaluation of teaching academic ability and psychological resilience development. This study conducted empirical verification in combination with the Yerkes-Dodson motivation-Efficiency inverted U theory. Based on semi-structured interviews with 14 participating university teachers and two rounds of questionnaire surveys, the study found that the competition pressure of the participating university teachers presented an "inverted U-shaped" distribution, with the peak pressure in the provincial competition selection stage being the highest (averaging 8.2 points). The psychological resilience of teachers presents a three-dimensional structure of "persistence-iteration-breakthrough," and its functional exertion is context-dependent. There is a "triple disconnection" in current psychological support-disconnection in timing, disconnection in form and disconnection in evaluation. The research further revealed the notable differences in stress perception and support needs among independent participating university teachers and teachers of different teaching ages. Based on the negative case analysis method, the conclusion of the singularity of psychological support was corrected, and the optimal pressure range of university teaching competitions was calculated through quantitative questionnaires. Based on this, this paper proposes a four-dimensional reform path for the "dual-track drive" institution-level (school-level) competition management model: hierarchical psychological intervention, personalized support principles, full-cycle resilience cultivation, and reconstruction of the evaluation mechanism. The research provides theoretical basis and practical path for the innovation of the management mode of teaching competitions for university teachers.

items.title: Mental health literacy status and its related factors among emergency nurses in public hospitals of Hubei Province: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Lu Z, Qiu H, Mei X, Ma N, Qin X, Tang Y, Zhang Q, Song Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Higher mental health literacy (MHL) among emergency nurses is associated with lower levels of work-related stress and burnout, as well as an enhanced ability to identify and address patients' psychological needs. However, current research on the MHL status of this group and its related factors remains insufficient.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: This study aims to assess the level of MHL among emergency department nurses and to identify the factors associated with it.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: A cross-sectional study.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: From June 2024 to September 2024, 221 participants were recruited from 10 public hospitals in Hubei Province. Data were collected using validated psychological instruments, including the Mental Health Literacy Scale, Basic Psychological Needs Scale, and Public Service Motivation Scale, along with demographic questionnaires. Statistical analyses were conducted using the Mann-Whitney U test, Kruskal-Wallis test, Spearman correlation analysis, random forest modeling, and multiple linear regression.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The results revealed that the standardized MHL score among emergency nurses was 69.0%. MHL showed significant positive correlations with public service motivation (PSM) and basic psychological needs (BPN). Random forest analysis indicated that the association between BPN and MHL had the highest relative importance among all predictors. Collectively, these variables contributed to the explanation of 41.4% of the variance in MHL.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Research suggests that the MHL of emergency nurses requires improvement. Both BPN and PSM were significantly correlated with MHL, with the correlation between BPN and MHL being stronger. However, the investigation reveals an imbalance within the emergency department nursing population, characterized by lower BPN scores and higher PSM scores.

items.title: The financial burden of climate disasters on household's health expenditure: evidence from Australia.
items.authors: Betancourt-Odio A, Fonseca M, Budría S.

sections.text: Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of natural disasters. While a growing literature documents their effects on psychological well-being, less is known about their implications for household medical expenditure. This study examines the relationship between direct exposure to weather-related disasters and out-of-pocket pharmaceutical expenditure. We use nationally representative longitudinal data from the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey covering 2009-2021. Individual fixed-effects models account for time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity and control for a rich set of socioeconomic and demographic characteristics. Exposure to weather-related disasters is associated with significantly higher out-of-pocket pharmaceutical expenditure. This association is concentrated among individuals without private health insurance. An analysis of potential transmission mechanisms further shows that disaster exposure increases the likelihood of reporting several physical and mental health conditions. The findings suggest that the economic costs of climate-related disasters extend beyond physical damage and public reconstruction spending, affecting household welfare through higher pharmaceutical expenditure. The concentration of this burden among individuals without private health insurance highlights the potential role of insurance coverage in shaping the financial consequences of climate-related shocks.

items.title: A descriptive analysis of Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act cases involving disruptive patient behavior, 2023.
items.authors: Reichert Z, Axeen S, Minasian A, Fedigan ANA, Cadet J, Ogele N, Khawaja Z, Seabury S, Menchine M, Pines JM, Terp S.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) requires emergency departments (EDs) to provide a medical screening examination (MSE) and stabilizing care regardless of ability to pay. While EMTALA protects access to care, its application can be challenging when patients are disruptive or violent. This study estimates the proportion of EMTALA citations for MSE deficiencies involving disruptive behavior and describes case characteristics.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a retrospective, descriptive analysis of Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) EMTALA citations for MSE deficiencies from 2023. We screened narrative inspection texts using predefined keywords, then manually reviewed them to identify disruptive behavior and assess whether it appeared willful. Case characteristics were recorded and described.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 227 EMTALA citations involving MSE deficiencies with narrative inspection reports available for review, 49 (21%) were determined to involve disruptive behavior. Common behaviors included verbal abuse, refusal of care, threats, and violence, most often directed at nurses. Ten cases (20%) were considered likely willful; the remainder stemmed from acute psychiatric conditions, intoxication, or medical illness.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Disruptive behaviors appear in a notable proportion of EMTALA citations for MSE deficiencies, highlighting the challenge of balancing regulatory compliance with staff safety and ED operations.

items.title: The Impact of Treatment With Pegvaliase on Quality of Life for Individuals With PKU.
items.authors: Heller T, Morand M, Roberts P, Hashmi SS, Northrup H, Falugi C, Richardson K.

sections.text: Management for phenylketonuria (PKU) has traditionally involved adhering to a strict low-protein diet to maintain phenylalanine (Phe) levels within the recommended range of < 360 μmol/L. The time commitment and financial, emotional, and social burdens of adhering to a restrictive diet, as well as the neurocognitive symptoms associated with elevated Phe levels, make it challenging to manage PKU and reduce quality of life (QoL). Pegvaliase is an enzyme substitution therapy used to lower blood Phe levels and allow for relaxation of Phe-restricted diets. Our study investigates the subjective impact of pegvaliase on QoL. We surveyed 34 individuals currently treated with pegvaliase regarding its impact on four domains of QoL: neurocognitive, emotional/psychiatric, social, and practical. There was a statistically significant improvement in every QoL domain addressed by this study after responding to pegvaliase ( p  < 0.05). The majority of participants agreed or strongly agreed that pegvaliase made daily life easier and that it improved their cognitive functioning, emotional wellbeing, physical health, and social interactions. QoL aspects that remained significant challenges post-pegvaliase included the financial burden and difficulty with insurance, feeling different or isolated from others, difficulty traveling, and strain in relationships with friends and family. The results of this study indicate that pegvaliase has an overall positive impact on QoL, including for participants with low initial Phe levels. Therefore, access to pegvaliase may be beneficial for a broader range of patients with PKU, even those with baseline Phe levels within the recommended range.

items.title: Endobronchial Foreign Body Diagnosed 15 Years After Aspiration and Successfully Removed: A Case Report.
items.authors: Anacleto A, Cuanda S, Sachicola O, Gonçalves E, Arrais M.

sections.text: Airway foreign body aspiration is a rare condition in adults and is generally associated with predisposing factors such as advanced age, alcoholism, mental health disorders or neurological impairment. Diagnosis is challenging when patients are unable to recall the aspiration event, which leads to delayed diagnosis and complications. We describe the case of a 30-year-old man with no history of disease who presented with recurrent cough and repeated respiratory infections; he had been treated with antibiotics on several occasions without improvement. Upon detailed questioning, he recalled having inhaled a foreign body (a soccer ball pump needle) at Age 15. A chest X-ray revealed a metallic foreign body measuring approximately 4 cm in length, lodged in the middle lobe, which was confirmed by bronchofibroscopy. The airway foreign body was removed via bronchofibroscopy without complications. The patient made a satisfactory recovery, and his respiratory symptoms resolved.

items.title: Brain-state dependence of neuromodulation: psychosocial stress aligns prefrontal perfusion dynamics during online tDCS.
items.authors: Wu GR, Wei L, De Wandel L, Van Schuerbeek P, Klooster D, Catoira B, Wang C, Horczak P, De Smet S, Chen Q, Raeymaekers H, De Mey J, Remue J, Lemmens G, Baeken C.

sections.text: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) shows broad therapeutic promise, yet high inter-individual variability limits its clinical efficacy. Here, we investigated whether pre-stimulation brain state reduces inter-individual variability in neural responses to online tDCS. Across two sham-controlled cohorts of healthy volunteers, we quantified cerebral blood flow (CBF)-based inter-subject correlation (ISC) during 20 minutes of active or sham tDCS (anodal left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, right supraorbital return). In our hypothesis-driven ROI analyses, following psychosocial stress induction (Study 1, N = 42; NCT07406503), active tDCS significantly synchronized perfusion trajectories (elevated ISC) within prefrontal and corresponding electric-field regions, while reducing synchrony in the pregenual anterior cingulate cortex. Crucially, this stress-dependent synchronization was absent during resting-state stimulation without prior stress exposure (Study 2, N = 43; NCT07406464). Exploratory whole-brain voxel-wise ISC and neurotransmitter-map association analyses further suggested that stress-state ISC modulations were preferentially aligned with normative cortical distributions of dopaminergic, noradrenergic, serotonergic, and GABAergic receptors, whereas such associations were not observed in the cohort without experimental stress induction. Although imaging modality differences (ASL vs. BOLD-fMRI) preclude attributing these divergences solely to stress, our findings demonstrate that psychosocial context shapes tDCS-induced neural synchrony, with exploratory evidence linking these effects to cortical neurotransmitter landscapes, providing a critical biological framework for state-sensitive and personalized psychiatric neuromodulation.
